name: ERA Fellowship
notes: Applied summer 2026 (rejected, 6000 applicants for 30 spots). Missed Sep 2026 deadline — IITM end-term exam same day. Next window likely early 2027. Strong fit for agentic evaluation angle. ERA targets catastrophic risk pathways — frame application accordingly, not as general AI ethics.

name: MATS Winter 2027
notes: OPEN NOW. Window: Aug 25 – Oct 31 2026 (AoE). Program runs Jan 19 – Apr 10 2027. 12 weeks, $19,200 stipend + $24k compute + housing + meals + travel. Berkeley and London, remote possible in some cases. International applicants eligible. No LLMs allowed in application responses — flag this. Decisions early-mid Nov 2026. Needs one public output first — Apart Research hackathon is the stepping stone.

name: Apart Research Sprints
notes: Immediate entry point. 3-day hackathon format. Pipeline: Sprint → Studio (5-20% of submissions, 4-6 weeks) → Fellowship (40% of Studio, 4-6 months). Current sprint: AI Incident Response (ran Sep 11-13 2026 — check next one). Do this before MATS application. Remote-friendly, global.

name: SPAR Spring 2027
notes: Fall 2026 closed. Spring 2027 applications open ~December 2026. Part-time remote, 5-40hrs/week, ~3 months. 130+ projects across technical safety, governance, policy, security. ~20% acceptance if you apply to 3-5 projects. Good parallel track alongside a job.

name: Astra Fellowship
notes: Technical AI safety. More research-focused than Generator. Better fit than Generator for Michael. Check current cycle dates.

name: Generator Residency
notes: Summer 2026 closed Apr 27. Next round not announced — expressed interest for next cohort. Non-research program — for ops/generalist builders. In-person Berkeley only. J-1 visa needed. $6k/mo stipend + housing + travel. Pipeline into AI safety orgs. Watch for 2027 cohort announcement.

name: Anthropic Fellows Program
notes: OPEN — rolling applications, next cohort Nov 2026. 4 months full-time. $3,850 USD/week stipend + ~$15k/month compute. In-person Berkeley or London. Work auth required in US/UK/Canada — NO visa sponsorship. This is a hard blocker unless Michael relocates or gets another visa route. 80% of fellows produce papers, 40% join Anthropic. No PhD required. Strong technical background expected. Check if remote cohort possible.

name: OpenAI Safety Fellowship
notes: 2026-27 cohort: deadline May 3 2026 (closed), program ran Sep 14 2026 – Feb 5 2027. New in 2026, pilot program. Watch for 2027-28 announcement. Priority areas: safety evaluation, agentic oversight, robustness, scalable mitigations. Empirically grounded technical work preferred.

name: Chevening Scholarship
notes: Covers UK university + return flights. Strongly favors work experience, no age cap — very strong fit given 20yr background. Deadline typically early November. Ireland/UK longer-term residency route possible post-fellowship. One of the highest-fit opportunities given Michael's profile.

name: GovAI Fellowship
org: Centre for the Governance of AI
notes: Policy/governance track. Less direct than MATS but relevant pipeline. Check current cycle.

name: LASR Labs
notes: London-based, technical safety research. Check current cohort timeline.

name: ML4Good Bootcamp
notes: 8-day fully paid in-person bootcamp. Summer 2026 deadline was July 1 (closed). Next round likely Jan-Feb 2027 for spring cohort. Technical track (ML safety) or Governance track. Asia/East Asia cohorts being added — check. Good entry point before MATS/ERA. 98% recommendation rate. Alumni at UK AISI, MATS, CeSIA.

name: CBAI Summer Research Fellowship
notes: Fully-funded 9-week research fellowship. $10k compute support per fellow. Extension up to 6 months. Open to undergrads, masters, PhDs, postdocs, and recent graduates transitioning into safety research. Technical safety, AI governance, and technical governance tracks. 2026 deadline was Apr 12 — watch for 2027 cycle. Alumni joined Goodfire and Redwood, published at NeurIPS/ICLR.

name: FAS AI Safety Policy Entrepreneurship Fellowship
notes: 2026 deadline was Sep 7 (closed). Part-time hybrid, 5hrs/week, Sep 30 2026 – Feb 28 2027. $5k stipend + $1k merit award. In-person retreats in California and Washington DC. Policy/governance focus — less direct fit for Michael's technical background. Watch for 2027 cycle.

name: Claude Corps Fellowship
notes: Cohort 3 starting Aug 2027 — applications open Sep 2026. Focus: societal challenges + AI tools. Selection based on hands-on AI comfort, learning speed, communication, self-direction. No specific background required. Less technical than Anthropic Fellows. Work auth in eligible countries likely required — check.
